questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing my study destination, I thought a lot about the country's culture. I wanted to go somewhere different from the Denmark, and then I landed in Italy. Their way of living is a bit different than from Denmark. They are not in a ‘rush' like we are in Denmark, they take their time to do things and they always have time to sit down and take a coffee or a cold drink after school.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My overall study abroad experience was great. I met a lot of new friends from different countries and cultures and I learned a lot about myself. It was refreshing to study at a new school with a different approach to teaching. Here you were not so much prepared to the classes, you were more listening to the professor and not asking a lot of questions. Furthermore, you got a new student group with new people there came with new perspectives and way of seeing things.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All around it was ok to find the information I needed upon arrival. But the information afterwards towards the school in Milan was a bit more difficult as you didn't know where to look for the information, and when you don't know what to look for, then you don't know if you need any information. Furthermore, there was just a lot of new information to deal with

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Well when I arrvied at my campus (place to stay during the semester) I was met by the campus's secretary, which didn't speak english, and after that I met with the campus's boss who provided me with more information - but again, he didn't really speak that good english.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Well, I was satisfied, by I find it hard to arrive at new place where you can't really communicate with people.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Depends on what you mean by options. But at campus I had a room where i could sleep and a kitchen which I shared with 400 other students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I was cooking in a kitchen where 400 other students also had access. I was hard to make food as you always were surrounded by a lot of people. Furthermore, I was always a mess, as people didn't clean up after themselves. At my room I had a refrigerator, where I could store food. So usually in the morning I was eating at my desk in my room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That you should be aware of that you can't eat like you do at home, and you should expect at lof of people cooking and eating with you and that maybe they don't clean up after themselves.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was ok. I had a bed to sleep in and a common kitchen. At the price range it was ok. But it was hard to sleep well, as i shard the bedroom with another roommate, and it was hard to make good food as I shared the kitchen with 400 people. Furthermore, I had to buy my own kitchen utensils, which I didn't knew before arrival. Furthermore, I had to buy my own router to have access to the internet in my room. My room got cleaned every second week - which wasn't that good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a fine process – I just used a portal where I could register my courses. And if I made any changes I could just make a new registration, which was fine. But the only thing I found difficult, was that you were not really provided with any information about when is the last time you can make a change.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You went on the host university's intranet and then you clicked on register your courses online and you went on a portal, where you could write the name of your courses and how many credits they were.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a guide where you could see how to do it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went really well. I did it right the first time - as i followed the guide.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the guide, and everything will be alright.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of my courses was ok. I took MA courses. The syllabus niveau and amount of pages to read was the same as in Denmark. But I found classes a bit different than from Denmark. I didn't have to engage in dicussions with the professor (I wasn't necessary) so i wasn't really challenged in the syllabus before the examines. But we had to do some presentations where we could discuss with the professor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Denmark, we dicuss a lot and we are prepared before the classes. At my host university, you don't know what to read before the examine and therefore you can't really dicuss the subjects.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advertising Communication
Digital Society
Behavioural Sociology
Introduction to R

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Digital Society. Here you could discuss a bit more with the teacher about the subjects and the course have a lot of new and interesting themes and subjects, which are up to date with the technology there are today. And I like how they connect technology with the society and we learn how it works together and affects each other.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't really expect any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think that transport was cheaper than expected. For around 16 euros each month you can use all the busses and metros inside the city.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really though about non-academic opportunities - so i can't really answer it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I knew that you could attend to some sports - but I didn't really thought about it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Arrange trips yourself!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other cities and experience the food and churches! There is a lot to come after!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some weeks. But I was really tired in the beginning. The most difficult thing to adjust to, was that I had to sleep with a roommate. Because of that, I went later to bed which was hard for me. Furterhmore, I was also hard in the beginning to adjust to the food.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with your classmates! They are opened minded and want to learn about who you are and where you are from!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sleeping later and eating later

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they taking things a lot easier. They are not in a rush. They always have time for a coffee or a drink during the week.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open minded!

Don't be afraid of talking with your classmates - they are probably in the same position as you are.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can't expect to know everything - as it's a new school and system you attend. But take it easy - everything will be okay.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, cultures and that I learned a lot about myself, as I was in a new country where my frames of living was challenged - in a good way!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I had to adjust to a "new" way of living in a country without my friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
